title: Explicit Retrieval, Implicit Cognition: Towards Personalized Micro-video Popularity Prediction via Dual Latent Memory

problem.claim: Micro-video popularity prediction supports product marketing and recommendation.

gap.claim: Existing approaches using independent modality encoders face a personalized reasoning bottleneck, losing grounding in multimodal evidence and personalized experience during reasoning.

contributions.claim: CLAMP synergizes a large multimodal model with dual latent memory: short-term content-centric perceptual retention and long-term user-centric semantic consolidation.
CLAMP uses familiarity-recollection memory retrieval with adaptive switching between fast recognition and deliberate chain-like episodic retrieval pathways.
CLAMP dynamically generates latent memory tokens and invokes them during inference to retain perceptual evidence and user-level semantics during thinking and generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show CLAMP consistently outperforms all baselines.
The authors report that the experiments validate CLAMP's efficacy in personalized micro-video popularity prediction reasoning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Micro-video popularity prediction is important for marketing and recommendation.
Existing modality-encoder approaches lack grounded and personalized reasoning.
CLAMP combines a multimodal model with short-term and long-term latent memory.
Adaptive familiarity-recollection retrieval and dynamic memory-token invocation preserve perceptual and personalized semantics during inference.
The authors report consistent improvement over all baselines in extensive experiments.
